newsitem.title: UK: London gold glued to range, silver eyes downside.
newsitem.headline: London gold glued to range, silver eyes downside.

text.p: Gold prices were at a virtual standstill on Tuesday, but the rest of the precious metals looked like testing slightly lower levels, dealers said.
"There's good selling at $382 so we're in a very tight range," a dealer said of the gold market. "Unless we can break it we're going to be here all week. It's very dull."
Bullion fixed unchanged from the morning's fixing at $381.00 an ounce. In New York, Comex December gold was down $0.70 at $383.10 an ounce.
Gains from a flicker higher overnight had rapidly evaporated and a flurry of buying early in the day disappeared.
The precious metals had surged higher last week in an effort to break out of a recent downtrend, but the momentum appeared to have worn off, dealers said.
Silver, which made the most dramatic move last week by racing above the key $5.00 an ounce level, was now testing out the floor within its new price rance.
"We may get a look at $4.98. I wouldn't be surprised to see it test the lows," a dealer said.
Prices were indicated at $5.01/$5.03 an ounce, a decline of three cents from Monday's London close, and a low bid was quoted so far at $4.99 an ounce.
The other white metals were also eyeing lower values.
Palladium fixed in the morning and afternoon at $116.25 an ounce, the lowest fixing since September 14, 1993. A low bid was quoted at $115.75.
Prices of the white metal, used primarily in electronics, catalytic converters and dentistry, have been declining steadily since rallying to a high of around $175 an ounce in April 1995.
Dealers attributed it slide in recent months to steady sales from key producer Russia and slack demand from the Japanese electronics industry.
"It's a continuation of that trend. I'ts being hit from both the supply and demand angles," a dealer said. "There hasn't been anything dramatic, it's just drifting off."
Recent attempts to claw above the important $120 an ounce resistance level have met with selling and the market has a distrinctly bearish cast to it, he added.
Analysts and dealers said palladium showed the potential to drop further still, towards support at $112 and then possibly below $100 an ounce.
Platinum was indicated $0.50 lower at $384.50/$385.50 an ounce, with a low bid quoted at $384.00.
